uncited: Projects the 3D vector onto the surface in the direction of the x and y components of the surface normal.
It is viewpoint-independent and designed for z-axis rotation.
Projects vectors parallel to the viewing direction.
* Time Complexity: Not given in the sources.
* Memory Complexity: Not given in the sources.
* When to use: When generating film loops with rotation about the z-axis for simple, axis-centered surfaces.
* When not to use: For complex surfaces not centered on the axis, or when uniformity of the vector field is the primary visualization goal.
Cylinder projection was introduced in the context of visualizing 3D velocity fields near contour surfaces.
